A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PepTune study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original peptide-generation experiments, trained property-prediction results, docking studies and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains these original computational experiments and adds a component-ablation study in Appendix I.2.

M1.justification: The reported guidance procedure changes substantively. V1 Equation 21 and Algorithm 4 select using normalized rewards alone; v4 Section 3 and Algorithm 5 add a denoiser-prior and visit-count exploration bonus with c=0.1. V4 also replaces stochastic rollout with explicit greedy argmax steps. Its documented procedure omits the search-time invalidity penalty specified in v1 Equation 34.

E1.justification: The training corpus and property-prediction datasets remain the same. Single-target studies for TfR, GLP-1R, GFAP, NCAM1 and AMHR2, dual-target TfR–GLAST and GFAP–RBX1 studies, and time-dependent guidance are retained across the main text and appendices. The new ablation introduces no additional dataset or biological task.

E2.justification: HELM-GPT, PeptideBERT, T7, semaglutide and liraglutide remain in their corresponding comparisons. V4 Table 13 adds two evaluated comparison variants: PepMDLM without bond-dependent masking and without invalidity loss. Comparator additions are confined to this component ablation.

E3.justification: V4 Table 13 introduces an ablation protocol that unconditionally samples 100 sequences per model and measures the fraction passing SMILES2PEPTIDE. The main benchmark metrics, model sizes, training budget and docking setup are otherwise retained. Omitted descriptions of existing settings do not establish that those settings changed.

E4.justification: V4 Appendix I.2 adds direct removal tests of bond-dependent masking and invalidity loss, providing substantially new evidence about the contributions of two central components. V1 lacks this component-level validity comparison. Its existing tokenizer, child-count, iteration-count and time-dependent guidance analyses are retained in v4 Appendices H and I.1.

E5.justification: Both versions retain standard-deviation shading in the TfR iteration plots, identified in v1 Figure 6 and v4 Figure 5. V4 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure; its new ablation reports point fractions only.

E6.justification: V4 Table 13 adds validity fractions of 0.40, 0.16 and 0.21 for the full model and its two ablations. V4 also omits v1's 36% validity statement for 200-token sequences and the 0.949 binding-affinity test correlation in Appendix C.2. Existing benchmark and docking tables retain their scores. The new 0.40 result does not establish a same-setting decline from the retained 0.45 benchmark.

T1.justification: V4 replaces the erroneous universal-dominance definition of the Pareto front in v1 Equation 20 with a non-dominance definition in Equation 11, and revises reverse-posterior algebra in Appendix B.1. The principal masking, NELBO and invalid-loss derivations already existed in v1; presenting them as Propositions 2.1–2.3 does not itself add new theory.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain peptide-SMILES discrete diffusion, bond-aware masking, invalidity loss, multi-objective tree guidance and property predictors, supporting chemically modified and multi-target peptide design. The MCTG name and stronger emphasis on inference-time guidance do not materially change the overall scientific claims.

C2.justification: V4 removes v1's substantive discussion of synthetic-data dependence, rare-residue synthesis complexity and costs, limited independent validation of non-binding properties, and ongoing in vitro assays. It also narrows the T7 interpretation from superior to similar binding properties and adds a rationale for preferring unrestricted Gumbel expansion over top-k sampling. These changes materially alter qualifications and mechanism explanations.

D1.justification: V4 supplies standalone reverse-diffusion-step pseudocode and the new exploration coefficient. However, it omits v1's binding-affinity split stratification and the 30K training-set description for APE tokenization. Most architecture tables, optimizer settings, hardware, training time, software versions and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds references including Coulom, Kingma et al., Ou et al. and newer discrete-generation work, and explicitly positions bond-dependent masking as extending Shi et al. It removes v1's discussion and citations of earlier molecular-generation applications of Pareto MCTS, AlphaDrug and ClickGen. The central positioning against structure-dependent design and gradient-based guidance remains.

P1.justification: V4 substantially rewrites and compresses the abstract, introduction and discussion, replacing the results-first narrative with methods-first sections. Most biological case studies and implementation material move into reorganized appendices A–J. Terminology changes from state-dependent masking and MCTS-based guidance to bond-dependent masking and MCTG.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format, with extensive relocation and resizing of figures and tables. Model schematics are revised, algorithms gain line numbers, and Table 13 is added. Most empirical plots and docking images are retained, while loss and perplexity direction arrows receive corrections.

improvement.justification: V4 adds useful component-ablation evidence, improves organization and corrects the Pareto-front definition. However, it removes important synthesis and experimental-validation limitations and some reproducibility details. Its substantially revised search procedure is not accompanied by evidence isolating the effects of those revisions, while principal benchmark results remain unchanged. These benefits and losses leave no reliably assessable net direction in overall paper quality.
